prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Buchwald and Hartwig turned aryl amination from a narrow, harsh transformation into a general, ligand-tunable operation, through rational ligand design (bulky biaryl phosphines, hindered alkylphosphines) backed by real mechanistic work on oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination. The evidence is structural and kinetic, not only synthetic. The method is used daily in pharmaceutical process chemistry, agrochemicals and organic electronic materials, so a whole community can now build what it could not before. Independent confirmation spans more than twenty-five years. The credit is the cleanest on the shortlist: two people who developed the decisive general catalysts independently and in parallel. The 2010 prize rewarded C-C coupling and left this area out.
statement.case_against: Some colleagues will say this is an extension of the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize and so less original. Kosugi and Migita's earlier tin-amide coupling is a real precursor, and Kosugi is credited on the ballot. A prize to Buchwald and Hartwig would also be a synthetic-methodology prize in a year when several members favour biology-facing chemistry with clearer paradigm change, and the field's best-known contribution is incremental ligand optimisation rather than a new concept.

responses.point: Somfai ranks B069 first and argues it is among the most heavily used bond constructions in process chemistry, that the generality and mechanism come from Buchwald and Hartwig, and that Kosugi and Migita are precursors.
responses.response: I agree on attribution and maturity. I would add that the decisive point for the citation is mechanistic: the ligand-design logic was tested against isolated intermediates and kinetics, which separates this from a mere scope expansion of 2010. I would not use Kosugi as a third laureate. The earlier tin-amide chemistry lacked the generality and the catalyst design, and adding a name would dilute a clean pair.

responses.point: Aili puts B045 (targeted protein degradation) first as event-driven pharmacology that hijacks the ubiquitin-proteasome system, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa as the core, and concedes that timing is arguable without an approved degrader.
responses.response: The idea is original and I take the impact seriously, but I disagree on readiness. Eight credited names and a crowded attribution mean any three-person cut leaves out real contributors, notably Ciulli on VHL ligands and structure-guided design and Gray on glue and kinase degraders. Ternary-complex structures are now plentiful, yet general rules for predicting productive degradation are not settled, and the strongest clinical evidence is still pending. I would rank it behind B069 now and revisit once a degrader is approved.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks B006 (long-range electron transfer in proteins, Gray and Winkler) first, valuing a quantitative physical framework tested in ruthenium-modified proteins, and sees the field as stable and not premature.
responses.response: I respect the quantitative rigour and agree that the two-person attribution is clean. My reservation is breadth of consequence. The framework is foundational for bioenergetics, but it is a mechanistic insight in a narrower community, and it builds on Marcus theory, recognised in 1992. The question for me is whether it enabled new capabilities for many chemists, and there B069 is stronger. I would not oppose B006 as the second achievement if the committee wants a two-part prize.

responses.point: The chair ranks B018 (dye-sensitised solar cells, Gratzel and O'Regan) first as a clear principle, separating light absorption from charge transport, with decades of confirmation and some commercial use.
responses.response: The principle is elegant and the 1991 paper is the decisive contribution, so I accept the attribution. Where I differ is on how far the original device concept reached. Practical impact has stayed in niches, and the energy-materials story has moved to perovskites, which grew from it. That makes B018 harder to justify than B069, whose practical use is broad and continuing.

uncertainties: How strongly the committee will treat the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize as covering C-N coupling.
Whether Kosugi or Migita should be credited, which depends on the precise priority chronology between the tin-amide work and the Buchwald and Hartwig reports; I am relying on memory for the details.
Whether a two-part prize pairing B069 with a second achievement would be preferable, given that the three-person limit would then force a single laureate for the second part.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B069, B054 or B013. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, which has no bearing on any shortlisted candidate. B013 touches on structural methods for small crystals, which is close to my own field of electron crystallography, but I have no personal or institutional tie to its credited names.
